sections.overview: This Sphingidae moth ranges from southern Texas into Mexico.
sections.identification: Grey-blue wings bear dark marks; wingspan is about 7–8.2 cm.
sections.habitat: It occurs in tropical and subtropical lowlands.
sections.diet: Host plants are unreported; adults probably take flower nectar.
sections.behavior: The consulted account does not report its flight season.
sections.reproduction: Mature caterpillars pupate in underground chambers.
sections.ecology: It is one of the recognized species in genus Sphinx. It ranges from south Texas into Mexico. Its congener Sphinx canadensis reaches Arkansas from Canada.
sections.conservation: BAMONA calls it a rare stray in the United States only.
